subsystems.name: Air contactor
subsystems.role: draws ambient air through a sorbent that captures carbon dioxide.
parts: sorbent material (solid amine or liquid solvent)

subsystems.name: Sorbent regeneration
subsystems.role: releases the captured CO2 and restores the sorbent for reuse.

subsystems.name: CO2 compression and purification
subsystems.role: compresses the CO2 stream to pipeline pressure and removes impurities.

subsystems.name: CO2 transport and injection
subsystems.role: moves compressed CO2 to a storage site and injects it underground.

subsystems.name: Energy supply
subsystems.role: provides the low-carbon heat and electricity the process needs.
parts: or natural gas with carbon capture

subsystems.name: Sorbent manufacturing
subsystems.role: produces sorbent material at the scale required for many plants.

buildSteps.title: Select site
buildSteps.detail: Find a location with abundant low-carbon energy, suitable geological storage, and enough land and water.

buildSteps.title: Build air contactor
buildSteps.detail: Construct large structures with fans and sorbent beds that can process vast volumes of air.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture sorbent
buildSteps.detail: Produce solid sorbents or liquid solvents in chemical plants, ensuring durability and low cost.

buildSteps.title: Install regeneration system
buildSteps.detail: Add heat exchangers, steam supply, and vacuum pumps to release CO2 and regenerate the sorbent.

buildSteps.title: Add compression and pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Compress the CO2 to pipeline pressure and build a pipeline to the storage site.

buildSteps.title: Develop storage
buildSteps.detail: Characterize deep geological formations, drill injection wells, and install monitoring.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and commission
buildSteps.detail: Connect the energy supply, test capture and storage, and begin continuous operation.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Replicate modules in mass production to reduce costs and reach megatonne and gigatonne scales.

prerequisites.why: DAC requires large amounts of heat and electricity; using fossil energy without capture would negate the climate benefit.
Proven at megatonne scale in saline aquifers and basalt formations, but capacity and distribution need characterization for gigatonne scale.
Thousands of kilometres operate today, but a gigatonne-scale effort requires a far larger network.
Current sorbents are costly and degrade; more durable, lower-cost materials are needed.
Contactors are large and complex; mass production is essential to reduce costs.

pathway.milestone: kilotonne-scale plants operating, such as Orca and Mammoth
pathway.unlocks: learning by doing, early cost reductions, and policy support

pathway.milestone: megatonne-scale plants under construction, such as Stratos
pathway.unlocks: supply chain development and integration with CO2 storage hubs

pathway.milestone: tens of megatonnes per year from multiple megatonne plants sharing infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: economies of scale and further cost reduction

pathway.milestone: gigatonne-scale deployment of hundreds of megatonne plants
pathway.unlocks: significant carbon removal to help meet climate goals
